Article Title: 'Congress hates tribal heroes': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi for skipping Birsa Munda tribute ceremony
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Sunday accused Congress of hating tribal heroes, saying that Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and his family skipped paying tribute to Birsa Munda at Parliament.In a social media post on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "Rahul Gandhi & Congress hates tribal heroes!""Rahul Gandhi & entire Gandhi Vadra family skipped paying tribute to Bhagwan Birsa Munda at Parliament! Recall how in the past Sonia Gandhi had called the President of India, who comes from a tribal background, a ‘poor lady’!" he added.Bhandari also targeted Rahul for attending the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, saying that the Congress leader had time for a summit with the George Soros ecosystem, but no time to pay respect to Bhagwan Birsa Munda."Rahul Gandhi has time for attending summit in Hyderabad with George Soros ecosystem, but no time to pay respect to Bhagwan Birsa Munda?" Bhandari questioned."Congress is anti tribal!" he added.This comes after President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, along with several Union ministers, paid floral tributes at the statue of Birsa Munda at Prerna Sthal in the Parliament House Complex on his 151st birth anniversary.Since 2021, November 15 has been observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas to honour the sacrifices of tribal freedom fighters and recognise the contributions of tribal communities to India's freedom struggle and national life.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "Rahul Gandhi & Congress hates tribal heroes!" This comes after President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, along with several Union ministers, paid floral tributes at the statue of Birsa Munda.

Article Title: ‘If PM Modi can offer Melody chocolates to Meloni ... ’: Sanjay Raut on Italian leader's remarks on Indian politics
Article Text:
Raut on European Socialist leader Giacomo Filibeck remarks

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Sunday took a sarcastic dig at the BJP over its criticism of Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck's remarks on Indian politics."If Modi can offer Melody chocolates to the Italian Prime Minister, then an Italian politician can come here and speak about this country," Raut said while speaking to reporters in Delhi."Democracy is being murdered in the country; this is a UN and human rights issue, not a matter involving any foreign power."His remarks came amid a political row over Filibeck's comments at the Congress-organised Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad, where the secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES) spoke in support of Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress.Filibeck had said democracy was "under attack" in India and called for international support to defend it. He also used the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod', popularised by Gandhi, drawing criticism from the BJP.The BJP accused the Congress of allowing foreign political representatives to comment on India's internal affairs and questioned their participation in the summit.

Article Title: 'Don't fall into BJP's trap': Raj Thackeray alleges bid to divide Mumbai over Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Raj Thackeray alleges BJP of 'divide and rule'

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena supremo Raj Thackeray on Thursday accused the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using Chhath Puja to create social and cultural tensions in Mumbai, urging people not to fall in a "political trap."In a post on X, Thackeray alleged that the BJP was attempting to provoke a confrontation between Marathi and North Indian communities ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. He claimed that the party and its social media network were circulating reels around Chhath Puja and what he termed cultural aggression to create discord in Maharashtra.Thackeray also referred to Bhojpuri songs being played at some railway stations in Mumbai, claiming that the MNS had intervened to stop the practice."However, the BJP appears to be disappointed that all these efforts have still not managed to create the kind of conflict it expects. And all this exercise is being undertaken with the upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections in mind," he said.Questioning the BJP's political strategy, the MNS chief said the party's think tank appeared to have run out of ideas and that its long-standing "divide and rule" formula would no longer help it win elections.He alleged that the BJP had repeatedly attempted to exploit religious and caste divisions for electoral gains, claiming that it sought to create Hindu-Muslim tensions ahead of Lok Sabha elections and caste-based divisions before state assembly polls."Whenever Lok Sabha elections approach, it tries to ignite Hindu-Muslim tensions. It brings Muslim women wearing burqas into playgrounds and gardens and attempts to scare people by saying, 'Look, look, now they have reached our playgrounds and gardens.' Of course, several videos of people wearing burqas to create an atmosphere of terror among Hindu women and men are already visible on social media," he said.Thackeray also cited the row surrounding Mumbai's Kabutarkhana, alleging that the BJP had attempted to fuel a Gujarati-versus-Marathi divide ahead of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation elections last year."I have said several times in my speeches that when the BJP realises it cannot win elections by showcasing its work, it creates conflict between two groups and wins elections on the bloodshed that follows," he said.He further alleged that the Election Commission played the decisive role in electoral victories, while communal and social conflicts were used by the BJP to explain its success.
Article Summary: Raj Thackeray accuses BJP of using Chhath Puja to create social and cultural tensions in Mumbai. MNS supremo urges people not to fall in a "political trap" He alleges that the BJP was attempting to provoke a confrontation between Marathi and North Indian communities.

Article Title: BJP's Hardeep Singh Puri resigns as Rajya Sabha member from Uttar Pradesh
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha Chairman accepts Hardeep Puri's resignation from UP seat after MP bypoll win

NEW DELHI: Senior BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri on Saturday resigned from his Rajya Sabha seat representing Uttar Pradesh , days after being elected unopposed to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh.According to a bulletin issued by the Rajya Sabha, Puri's resignation has been accepted by the chairman with effect from November 14.The bulletin stated, "Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, an elected Member of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), representing the State of Uttar Pradesh, resigned his seat in the Rajya Sabha and his resignation has been accepted by the Chairman, Rajya Sabha w.e.f. 14th November, 2026."Puri was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh last week after the nomination papers of two other candidates were rejected, leaving him as the sole contender in the by-election.The Madhya Pradesh seat had fallen vacant following the resignation of former Union minister of state L Murugan .
Article Summary: Senior BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri on Saturday resigned from his Rajya Sabha seat representing Uttar Pradesh. Puri's resignation has been accepted by the chairman with effect from November 14. He was elected unopposed to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh last week.

Article Title: 'Exposes BJP's tall claims that everything is hunky-dory': Congress on recent J&K attacks
Article Text:
Cong chief alleged that the Centre tried to project an image of peace in J&K.

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir Congress chief Tariq Karra on Saturday said recent attacks in the Valley had exposed the Centre's "tall claims of peace" and that "everything is hunky-dory" in the Union Territory.Speaking to reporters at a party function marking the birth anniversary of India’s first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, Karra cited the attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam and the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar as evidence that the security situation remained a concern.He criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for citing open markets, functioning schools and the absence of strikes or stone-pelting as signs of normalcy in Kashmir, alleging that such claims overlooked the situation on the ground."Whenever something like this happens, the government of India stands in the dock. You must have heard repeatedly, both inside and outside Parliament, whether it is the prime minister or the home minister; when it suits them, they say Kashmir is very peaceful, and nothing happens there," he said.Karra alleged that the Centre tried to project an image of peace internationally but was exposed by its "poor performance and wrong policies"."Such incidents expose the tall claims of the BJP , including those of the prime minister and home minister, that everything is hunky-dory... It (attacks) is a failure of the security apparatus and the policies adopted by the government of India," he said."The Centre forgets that this is a deceptive calm. If this is not a deceptive calm, then how do such incidents happen?" he added.Karra’s remarks came days after terrorists riding a motorcycle opened fire on CRPF personnel at a checkpoint in Kulgam district on Wednesday afternoon, injuring three security personnel.The attack took place around 2.15 pm, when the assailants fired at the personnel before fleeing, officials said. The injured were taken to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment.In a separate incident in Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of two SPOs who had gone missing on Wednesday were recovered on Thursday morning. The two personnel went missing while travelling from their camp towards an Army post at Dharna-Marwah on Wednesday.When asked about actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut’s remarks on Congress leader Sonia Gandhi ’s book, Karra said he did not take Ranaut seriously. He said the comments reflected a lack of political maturity, culture and values.He added that the remarks would neither diminish Gandhi’s stature and respect nor weaken her resolve to revive democracy in the country. "The BJP and its mindset is getting exposed, that's all," he said.Paying tribute to Nehru, Karra described him as one of the senior-most leaders of modern India, saying he had made great sacrifices for the country’s independence.He said Nehru laid the foundation of modern India, a legacy later carried forward by Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi and other Congress leaders. Karra said Indian democracy was once admired and followed by countries around the world, but alleged that the BJP had weakened the democratic system.
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir Congress chief Tariq Karra said recent attacks in the Valley had exposed the Centre's "tall claims of peace" Karra cited the attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam and the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar.

Article Title: SAD, BJP seat-sharing talks under way; formal announcement expected this month: Report
Article Text:
The former allies are discussing a possible reunion ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are holding discussions on seat-sharing for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, with a formal announcement on a possible alliance expected later this month, news agency PTI reported on Saturday, citing sources from both parties.The talks come amid growing speculation that the former allies could reunite after ending their decades-old partnership in 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws.Union Jal Shakti minister and BJP's Punjab election in-charge C R Patil is expected to visit the state on November 17 and meet party leaders in Chandigarh, PTI reported citing sources. His visit comes as discussions around a possible alliance gain momentum.The speculation has also intensified following recent political engagements. Former Punjab chief minister Amarinder Singh met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi a few days ago and is learnt to have discussed issues concerning the state, including drug abuse.The two parties had shared power and contested elections together for several years before the SAD walked out of the alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws.Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement for Punjab Assembly elections, the SAD contested 94 seats and the BJP 23 of the state's 117 constituencies. In Lok Sabha polls, the SAD contested 10 seats and the BJP three.The BJP has since indicated that it is no longer willing to play a junior partner in Punjab and has maintained that it is preparing to contest all 117 assembly seats.In the 2022 Punjab assembly elections, the BJP won two seats, while the SAD secured three. The next assembly polls are due in 2027.
Article Summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are holding discussions on seat-sharing for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The talks come amid growing speculation that the former allies could reunite after ending their decades-old partnership in 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws.

KOLKATA: Trinamool national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee was questioned by Bhowanipore police for nearly four hours on Saturday in connection with an FIR for his social media post against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Banerjee arrived at 12.23 pm, seven minutes ahead of his scheduled summons, and left around 4.30 pm. Police sources said his response was being studied and he might be called again if needed.BJP workers raised “chor” (thief) slogans while Banerjee was inside. As he emerged from the police station, TMC supporters countered by accusing BJP of paying demonstrators to shout slogans, and attacked state govt over high unemployment and delay in the Annapurna scheme’s rollout.Banerjee was summoned in a May 27 FIR filed by one Arnabkanti Das, who alleged that in his May 2 post on X, the MP described CEC Kumar as a “puppet of an anti-Bengali Gujarati gang”.Police booked Banerjee under BNS provisions relating to promoting enmity, inciting violence, spreading rumours, provoking offences against the state and causing public disorder.Speaking to reporters after the questioning, Banerjee said: “Whenever officials have summoned me, I have gone.I am being called in various false cases. I am appearing because of the high court’s directive. If they call me again, I will go. Based on one post, they questioned me as much as they wanted and I cooperated.”The TMC MP also claimed to have explained why he said “Gujarati gang”. “BJP believes Bengali is not even a language; they say there is only a Bangladeshi language. Amit Malviya had called Bengali a Bangladeshi language,” he added.Banerjee also launched a sharp attack on CM Suvendu Adhikari, asking why he had not faced similar summons in the Narada case.Addressing the recent demolition drive outside his residence, Banerjee said while he did not object to the removal of govt structures or police camps, authorities must not jeopardise the livelihoods of local artisans. “Please do not evict those who are working along the footpaths here. If you want to run a bulldozer, run it over my house.If you want revenge, take it on me, because you cannot fight me politically,” he said.State minister Dilip Ghosh, reacting to Banerjee’s appearance before the police, said: “He has been summoned multiple times by ED, CBI and others earlier as well. This saga will continue.”Trinamool had failed to shed its “feudal” mindset even after its electoral defeat, Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said, adding: “There is a saying ‘.”Banerjee has also been summoned by Girish Park police on Nov 20 in a separate FIR over derogatory remarks and threats against a serving officer in the state.
Article Summary: Banerjee arrived at 12.23 pm, seven minutes ahead of his scheduled summons, and left around 4.30 pm. Police sources said his response was being studied and he might be called again if needed. Banerjee was summoned in a May 27 FIR filed by one Arnabkanti Das.

NEW DELHI: An 82-year-old man died after being hit by a tractor in southwest Delhi's Chhawla Friday night. Police suspect that the elderly man was crossing the road when the vehicle struck him. The tractor driver allegedly fled the spot and is yet to be arrested.The deceased was identified as Banarasi Ram, a retired Armyman who lived with his family in Chhawla. According to police, the incident took place around 10.20pm in Pandwalan Khurd. A PCR vehicle passing through the area spotted the injured man and took him to a nearby hospital, where he was declared dead. The PCR staff informed the local police.Police have seized the tractor. It belonged to a person from Ujwa village in Dwarka, sources said. Several teams are trying to identify and trace the driver. Investigators are examining various factors that might have led to the accident, including speeding, visibility and lighting conditions on the road.A case has been registered under sections 281 (rash driving or riding on a public way) and 106(1) (causing death by negligence) of BNS.The incident comes on the same day as another fatal road accident involving an elderly woman in west Delhi's Inderpuri. The 68-year-old woman was hit by a scooter and subsequently struck by another vehicle while crossing a road around 11am Friday. Two persons were arrested Saturday.
Article Summary: An 82-year-old man died after being hit by a tractor in southwest Delhi's Chhawla Friday night. Police suspect that the elderly man was crossing the road when the vehicle struck him. The tractor driver allegedly fled the spot and is yet to be arrested.

Dhiraj is the son of former chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh.At the centre of the rift is cooperation minister and NCP member Babasaheb Patil, who broke ranks with the alliance and backed the Congress panel. In Oct, Patil rejected Mahayuti’s plan for a united contest, saying, “I had a 40-year association with the Congress panel. Moreover, cooperative elections are not fought on party symbols.”Patil later attended the nomination filing of Congress-panel candidate Avinash Patil from the Ahmedpur society constituency, making his stand public.BJP responded sharply. Former minister Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar alleged that Patil had aligned with Dhiraj Deshmukh and raised the issue with NCP leadership, seeking action against the minister. It has promised new branches in every taluka, interest-free marriage loans, education loans and full computerisation.Parivartan Panel has challenged several of those claims, particularly on interest-free farmer loans, and positioned itself as an alternative focused on farmers’ interests.The election will determine control of a key cooperative institution in drought-prone Latur and test whether Mahayuti can maintain local cohesion after one of its own ministers sided with the opposition. A total of 999 voters will elect 19 directors. Thirty candidates are in the fray, while four have already been elected unopposed.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Rejection, and subsequent restoration, of Sumit Patil’s nomination has become the central flashpoint in the Jalgaon District Central Cooperative Bank election, scheduled for Nov 29.The decision has ended the prospect of an unopposed victory for BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde in Pachora and sharpened tensions within the ruling Mahayuti alliance. Sumit is the son of Pachora Shiv Sena MLA Kishor Patil.A senior Shiv Sena functionary said that with Sumit back in the fray, the key BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde’s prospects of an unopposed victory from Pachora have now been dashed.The Mahayuti alliance aims to contest unitedly, but seat-sharing friction has stalled a final agreement. At a meeting in Jalgaon attended by Girish Mahajan, Gulabrao Patil and NCP leaders, BJP demanded the largest share of nine seats. The deadlock continues over Muktainagar, Bhadgaon, Raver and Chopda, compounded by Kishor Patil’s absence from the meeting.The crisis began on Nov 3 when returning officer Manoj Chaudhary disqualified Sumit, prompting Kishor Patil to state that there are invisible forces working against his family.Sumit challenged the rejection before the divisional joint registrar of cooperatives in Nashik. The appellate authority overturned the returning officer’s order and declared his nomination valid, allowing him to re-enter the electoral contestWith over 300 candidates in the fray and none withdrawing, the contest intensified for the 21-member board of directors for the 2026-2031 term, comprising 15 taluka representatives and six reserved seats.Over 3,000 eligible voters make up the electoral roll. Heavyweights including Union minister Raksha Khadse, ministers Girish Mahajan and Gulabrao Patil, and MLA Mangesh Chavan entered the fray.A senior BJP member said the development underscored how North Maharashtra’s cooperative sector was losing its traditional grassroots ethos to aggressive party politics. In Parola and Erandol, Nalini Patil, mother of MLA Amol Patil, and Mrunal Patil, Amol Patil’s wife, along with Rajani Savkare, wife of textile minister Sanjay Savkare in Bhusawal, secured unopposed victories.On the opposition front, the Maha Vikas Aghadi fielded an independent panel. Former MP and BJP state vice-president Sujay Vikhe Patil was elected unopposed as chairperson of the Ahilyanagar District Central Cooperative Bank on Thursday, following a rare alliance between political rivals — guardian and water resources minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil and former revenue minister Balasaheb Thorat.Ranjitsinh Deshmukh was elected unopposed as vice-chairperson. Defending the alliance, Thorat said farmers’ welfare outweighed politics amid drought conditions.“The district bank belongs to the common man and must survive.Given the drought-like situation, we kept politics aside and came together to work for farmers,” Thorat said.Meanwhile, Lanke, the lone opposition director who skipped the election process and signed the attendance register after arriving late, vowed to act as a strict watchdog. Declining to comment on internal backing, he said that the majority holds the right to decide.“I am alone in the opposition in the bank. I am the chowkidaar (watchman). If only my farmer survives will the sugar industry survive,” he added.

Madurai: Madras high court has directed the state to ensure that all wards in Govt Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai are provided with mosquito nets within six months.A division bench of Justice P Velmurugan and Justice K K Ramakrishnan was hearing a public interest litigation filed by A V Kathir of Madurai seeking a direction to the authorities for procurement of equipment for the cardiology department at GRH.The bench observed that the petitioner is a student pursuing his collegiate education in Bengaluru and is presently residing outside Tamil Nadu. The court is of the considered opinion that he is not entitled to maintain the present public interest litigation. Accordingly, the petition was liable to be dismissed on the ground of locus standi, the judges observed.However, considering the larger public interest involved in the matter, particularly with regard to the facilities and amenities available at GRH, the court is inclined to issue certain directions to the authorities, the judges observed. Taking into account the official submissions, the judges directed the authorities to ensure that all the wards of GRH are provided with mosquito nets within six months and file a compliance report before the court.The judges further directed the authorities to submit a detailed report within 15 days on the medical equipment and other essential amenities required for the effective functioning of GRH and the equipment and amenities already available at the hospital. The court adjourned the case to Dec 4 for filing the report.
Article Summary: Madras high court has directed the state to ensure that all wards in Govt Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai are provided with mosquito nets within six months. Article Title: Temple should be allowed to light Karthigai deepam at deepathoon: BJP
Article Text:

Madurai: BJP Tamil Nadu chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy has said that the temple should be allowed to light Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill without further obstruction in line with Madras high court ’s directions.In a statement, he said the state govt’s counter-affidavit before Supreme Court on Nov 12, opposing the plea for ASI involvement and permanent lighting of Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon, was unnecessary and seeks to reopen issues already settled by Madras HC. In Dec 2025, Justice G R Swaminathan directed the temple management to light the deepam at the deepathoon. The order was confirmed by a division bench in Jan 2026. The state itself filed an SLP against them only on June 11, on which Supreme Court issued notice but refused to stay the high court directions.He said the fresh counter affidavit continues to rely on the older 1996 directions, insists that the deepathoon is not a traditional site, and resists any meaningful ASI role beyond limited protection of the cave and inscriptions. This directly contradicts the specific and later findings of the high court, which already recognised ASI’s protective role over the hill.He said the TVK govt appears to be following the same approach earlier followed by DMK, prioritising minority vote banks even when it means obstructing the majority’s long-standing religious practices on temple-owned land. There is nothing wrong with protecting minority rights or ensuring communal harmony. However, that cannot be done by repeatedly hurting the religious sentiments of the majority and denying a temple the right to perform its rituals on its own property, he added.
Article Summary: BJP Tamil Nadu chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy has said that the temple should be allowed to light Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon. He said the state govt’s counter-affidavit before Supreme Court on Nov 12 was unnecessary and seeks to reopen issues already settled by Madras HC.
